targets.title: ERN and the placebo: a misattribution approach to studying the arousal properties of the error-related negativity.
targets.evidence_quote: Therefore, the aim of the present study was to investigate whether an experimental manipulation of the misattribution of state-anxiety following errors modulates the ERN/Ne. To this end, we aimed at replicating the findings of Inzlicht and Al-Khindi (2012).
targets.outcome_quote: As Inzlicht and Al-Khindi (2012), we did not observe performance differences between both groups. However, ERN/Ne differences between misattribution and control group could not be replicated, although the statistical power of the replication study was high. Evidence regarding the replication of performance and the non-replication of ERN/Ne findings was confirmed by Bayesian statistics.
targets.outcome_reasoning: Explicit comparison confirms the original null performance finding but fails the ERN/Ne effect. The introduction expressly says replication of the null performance result is as important as replication of the ERN/Ne result; thus both are planned target findings. There is no overall verdict overriding these contrasting comparisons. The terminology reproducibility refers here to a new sample, not reanalysis of original data.

reasoning: New randomized sample of 99 participants retests the original placebo-misattribution experiment. Title and all three authors match the JATS article front matter. The original reference is directly printed in the full text. Other arousal and ERN references provide context rather than additional independently retested originals.
